texts.preamble: Prashanta Kumar Sahoo vs State Of Odisha And Others .... Opp. ... on 25 April, 2025
texts.facts: He is running his business for more than ten years. He has also made an application for issuance of Street Vending Certificate on 23rd February, 2025 in Form-II under Paragraph-6(2) the Scheme framed under the provisions of the Act. The said application is pending before the Town Vending Committee, BMC-Opposite Party No.3. When the matter stood thus, the BMC is contemplating his eviction along with other similarly placed vendors. This Court in several other matters entertaining the writ petition, directed the Town Vending Committee, BMC to take a decision on the application for grant/renewal of certificate of Street Vending.
texts.arguments: The Petitioner in this writ petition prays for protection of his occupation over the space where he is running business and earning his livelihood. 3. Mr. Das, learned counsel submits that the Petitioner is a Street Vendor within the meaning of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 (for brevity 'the Act') and Rules as well as Scheme framed thereunder. Hence, Mr. Das, learned counsel submits that the case of the Petitioner may be considered by the Town Vending Committee, BMC and till it is considered, his possession over the space be protected to save him from penury. 4. Mr. Panda, learned counsel for BMC vehemently objects to the same. It is his submission that the Petitioner was never issued with any certificate of Street Vending under the provisions of the Act. He further submits that due to unauthorized occupation of the Petitioner and some other similarly placed vendors, there is traffic congestion and BMC is facing difficulty in sanitation work. Further, the nature of business is not coming under the provisions of the Act, Rules Designation: Senior Stenographer Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Date: 25-Apr-2025 13:01:26 and Scheme framed thereunder.
